subject: FRED adapter always times out at 8s use-case budget — design mismatch, not a regression

finding.symptom: fred.status = timeout on every POST /macro/external call. Container logs: '[FetchExternalMacroUseCase] fred timed out after 8000ms'.
finding.root_cause: FredMacroAdapter.fetchAllMacro() fetches 8 series SEQUENTIALLY with 0.6-1s sleep between each (fred-macro.ts:113-115). Minimum wall-clock time = 8 × (network_latency + ~0.8s sleep). The use-case budget for fred is 8000ms (fetch-external-macro.ts:51). Even with sub-1s network, 8 sequential calls with sleep gaps cannot fit in 8s. The adapter's own AbortSignal timeout is 10s per series, so the first fetch alone can exhaust the budget.
finding.confirmed_not_regression: fred-macro.ts was NOT modified in task/macro-scrapers-curl-cffi-upgrade. git log main..HEAD -- apps/macro-indicators/src/infrastructure/scrapers/fred-macro.ts returns empty. Budget line in fetch-external-macro.ts: only whitespace change (no value change). This was already timing out before the curl-cffi upgrade — notebook from prior QA session (macro-external-allsettled-timeout) confirms 'FRED HTTP 500 (API errors)' at that time.
finding.prior_live_state: ops-vps-fetch notebook notes FEDFUNDS=3.64 fetched from VPS. That was a direct VPS FRED API call, not via the macro-indicators container. Container-side FRED has always been limited by the 8s budget vs sequential fetch design.

recommendation.fix: Either (a) raise fred use-case budget to 90s to cover 8 × (10s timeout + 1s sleep), or (b) rewrite fetchAllMacro() to batch-parallel with Promise.all (same technique as yahoo/cnbc/tradingEconomics upgrade — this branch shows the pattern), or (c) use FRED bulk API endpoint to get all series in one call.
recommendation.priority: low — FRED was already non-functional in the container; no regression. Upgrade already tracked as follow-up work.

merge_impact: DO NOT BLOCK — this task/macro-scrapers-curl-cffi-upgrade branch does not touch FRED. File as separate follow-up task.
